Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Decant (development version)

  • New, experimental: chirp(), ambient-aware ligand-receptor calls. A ligand made by the cell type that dominates the soup is detected in every cluster, so a detection rule (>= 10% of cells) reports every cluster as a sender. chirp() calls a gene in a cluster only when its count is significantly above margin times the ambient count expected there, and scores pairs on the excess. Simulated ground truth only (2 seeds, rho 0.05-0.3): the detection rule called 600-950 absent pairs, chirp() none, and it found every pair expressed at >= 20 per 10k. It misses most pairs at 5-20 per 10k. With rho at 2/3 of its value it still made no false calls; at 1/2 it made up to 100. Since the contamination estimate is known to run low on some real data (1f below), check ambient_share_ligand before trusting a call. Not yet tested on real data. Correcting counts with bayes_cell and then applying the detection rule left 70-388 of those false calls on the same simulations; subtract left all of them, since its fractional counts still count as detected.

  • Second pre-registered real-data DE test: null. Paired brain regions (GSE272082, hippocampus or entorhinal cortex vs prefrontal cortex, within donors): standard edgeR called no gene foreign to microglia, so there was nothing for ambient_de to remove (validation/BENCHMARK.md 3d). In microglia EC vs PFC, ambient_de had a one-gene hit in 8 of 15 label swaps, above the pre-stated limit.

  • ambient_de(): robust weights are kept finite and positive (a NaN or infinite Pearson residual made edgeR stop on real data).

  • Contamination estimate on the 10k mixture: diagnosed, not fixed. The absent-gene fixed point collapses there (1 to 6 absent genes kept of 5,000+) because its overdispersion term starts at zero and its low start settles on the soup’s most abundant genes. A fallback start that fixed the 10k mixture failed on held-out data (hgmm 5k median 43% low, Spearman 0.49) and turned the negative control’s correct near-zero into NA, so the estimator is unchanged (validation/BENCHMARK.md 1f). validate_species_mixture.R now records a method that declines (rho NA).

  • Ambient removal: held-out results, and a change that did not pass. On held-out human/mouse mixtures (hgmm 1k, 5k, 10k) Decant removes 0.444 of ambient signal against DecontX 0.637 and SoupX 0.679, while keeping the most (retain 0.992). On the 20k mixture the loss was traced to bayes_cell’s cap, which keeps every single count of a gene with a tiny ambient expectation. Correcting that test for the number of cells (cap_test = "cluster", opt-in) raised held-out removal to 0.519 but dropped retain to 0.974 on the 10k mixture, so it is not the default (validation/BENCHMARK.md 1e). The larger part of the held-out gap comes from contamination estimates that are too low on those mixtures.

  • ambient_de() guards against implausible ambient fractions. A single cell type’s pseudobulk cannot always identify its own ambient fraction. On GSE273597 (pancreas) six donors’ ductal values came out at 0.86 to 0.96 and shuffled labellings gave up to 2,300 false hits. A sample above the new max_rho (0.5) now takes the median of the plausible samples, with their spread added to its uncertainty, and ambient_de warns (attr(res, "samples")$ambient_frac_imputed). Ductal shuffles: 4 of 24 with a hit, at most 1 gene. GSE190015 and GSE272082 unchanged. The pancreas data found the problem, so they do not validate the guard elsewhere.

  • Pre-registered real-data test (validation/BENCHMARK.md 3c): null. On T1D vs non-diabetic pancreas, naive edgeR found no ambient-driven hits to remove. ambient_de is now described as experimental in the README.

  • ambient_de() is now calibrated on real data. It fitted each gene with edgeR’s tagwise NB dispersion and then ran a quasi-likelihood F-test, which estimates the gene’s extra variance again: the variance was counted twice and the test was liberal. It now uses the trended dispersion, as edgeR’s quasi-likelihood pipeline does (dispersion = "trended"; "tagwise" restores the old behaviour). With condition labels shuffled between donors on two real datasets, the old default reported genes in 82 of 96 tests (up to 574 genes), the new one in 9 (at most 9 genes), naive edgeR in 4. GSE190015 (nine controls) was held out from the diagnosis. The simulation gates still pass with unchanged power. Re-run analyses made with earlier versions. joint_rho, first suspected, was not the cause. New: validation/validate_de_calibration.R, validation/BENCHMARK.md 3b.

  • Contamination estimate no longer halved on real data. Genes a cluster does not express scatter around rho by about 25-30% from gene to gene, far more than Poisson noise. estimate_rho_cluster() tested them against a Poisson, rejected the absent genes above the current rho and kept those below, and settled near the bottom of their spread. It now uses a negative binomial whose extra variance is estimated from the lower tail of the absent genes (overdispersed = TRUE). On a 20k human/mouse mixture the median rho went from 0.013 to 0.027 (truth 0.029) and ambient removal from 0.415 to 0.616. On further mixtures (validation/BENCHMARK.md, 1d) it has the lowest error of Decant, SoupX and DecontX on 1k and 5k cells, but still underestimates on 10k cells, where DecontX ranks cells better.

  • rho = 0 trap fixed. With sparse counts the starting value could be 0, which the fixed point cannot leave; on a 1k-cell mixture 7 of 8 clusters returned exactly 0. The start is now at least floor_rho.

  • Unidentifiable contamination is reported. When the soup resembles the cells (a single cell type), no gene is absent and rho cannot be estimated; the estimator returned 0.5-0.94 for a true 0.004 without a warning. Clusters above max_rho = 0.5 are flagged implausible and borrow rho from the others; when most cells are in such clusters decant() warns that rho is not identifiable and should be supplied ($rho_unidentifiable).

  • $rho_diagnostics gains dispersion and implausible columns.

  • The placeholder-name note is removed from DESCRIPTION: no CRAN or Bioconductor package is called Decant.

  • New user guide in 13 chapters (wiki/, also published as website articles). Every example runs on the bundled simulators, and scripts/check_user_guide.R checks that each shown output is current.

  • Scripts renamed for clarity: repository-level scripts moved to scripts/ (run_falsification_gates.R, compare_correction_methods.R, demo_structured_soup.R, stress_test_empty_mismatch.R); validation scripts follow benchmark_* (Decant against other tools) and validate_* (Decant against ground truth); result files renamed to match.

  • New correction rule "bayes_cell", now the default in decant(). "bayes" scaled every cell of a cluster by one ratio, so a cell whose count of a gene was far too high to be ambient (a doublet) lost most of it and inflated the cluster’s native profile. "bayes_cell" removes only the expected ambient from such entries and builds the profile from the rest. It has the lowest error in gate_correction() (0.065, against 0.071 to 0.075). On real PBMC data it removes 88 to 95% of ambient-compatible foreign marker counts (previously 84 to 94%) and 14 to 37% of the incompatible ones (previously 82 to 98%), at the same native loss.

  • validation/benchmark_pbmc_six_tools.R splits foreign marker counts into those ambient RNA could and could not have produced. DecontX removes both (96 to 100% of the incompatible ones).

  • New validation/benchmark_pbmc_six_tools.R and validation/py/run_python_tools.py: Decant against SoupX, DecontX, CellBender, scAR and AmbiDose on real PBMC data. DecontX removes more foreign marker signal than Decant; scAR adds counts and removes 44% of UMIs; Decant is the fastest. See validation/BENCHMARK.md.

  • Bug fix, found on real data. estimate_rho_cluster() overestimated rho several-fold on real 10x data (median 0.22 on PBMC 4k, where SoupX gives 0.06 to 0.077). Low-count genes passed the absent-gene test for lack of power. The absent set now requires an expected ambient count of at least min_expected = 5; the PBMC estimate is 0.063 (median).

  • decant() now defaults to correction = "bayes": on the PBMC data it removed 83 to 94% of marker counts from cell types that do not express them, against 19 to 57% for subtract.

  • Genes present in the empties but absent from every cell are dropped from the soup (floor_rho), and reported in the mismatch warning.

  • The two-sided soup/cell mismatch tripwire is retired: it raised a false alarm on the PBMC data. soup_mismatch now means more than 5% of the soup was in soup-only genes. Empties that over-represent genes the cells do contain are no longer flagged; this is a known limitation.

  • A cluster that cannot identify its own rho borrows the weighted median of the others, not a count-weighted mean.

  • New validation/validate_pbmc_markers.R, the first validation run on real data.

  • New validation/benchmark_soupx.R and validation/BENCHMARK.md: Decant against the official SoupX on real PBMC and simulated data, with the literature and what is and is not new. With the bayes default, correcting with Decant and then running edgeR matches ambient_de on the simulated 6 vs 6 study.

  • ambient_de() gains robust = TRUE (default): outlier samples are down-weighted per gene by Huber weights, the dispersion is re-estimated under them, and the residual degrees of freedom are reduced to match. Without it, cohorts of 50 or more samples per group with a few extreme counts gave 16 to 41% false positives on null genes (the failure Li et al. 2022 report for NB tests). DecantDE() inherits the default.

  • ambient_de() estimates the ambient term more accurately:

    • joint_rho = TRUE: each sample’s ambient fraction is refined on genes that look absent across all samples pooled, which removes an upward bias of about one point; its sampling variance now enters the model.
    • soup_design = TRUE, and soup_eb(design = ): soups are shrunk toward the design-fitted soup, not a condition-blind mean.

  • ambient_de(max_ambient_frac = 0.75): genes whose counts are mostly soup are not tested and are listed in attribute "ambient_dominated". Previously most such genes were dropped only as a side effect of the over-estimated ambient fraction.

  • ambient_de(lfc = ): test against a minimum fold change (as limma’s TREAT), for cohorts large enough that sub-1% biases become significant.

  • New simulate_ambient_cohort() and gate_ambient_de_cohort(): large cohorts with outlier samples, heavy-tailed noise, or a confounding batch.

  • scripts/run_falsification_gates.R exits non-zero when a required gate fails; CI runs each gate once.

  • experiments/large_cohort_calibration/: sweep over 6 to 200 samples per group, with its limits.

  • New validation/benchmark_differential_expression.R: contamination-aware DE against correct-then-test with the official SoupX, DecontX, FastCAR and CellBender (each run only if installed). Wrappers live in validation/comparators.R.

  • README: the claim that correcting counts first does not stop DE leakage is narrowed. It holds for Decant’s default subtract rule; official SoupX followed by edgeR removes almost all leakage on the simulator.

  • New vignette, “Contamination-aware differential expression”.

  • pkgdown site configuration and deployment workflow.

  • DESCRIPTION: URL, BugReports, biocViews, VignetteBuilder.
